function.name: generate_sea_foam
function.description: Simulates the creation of sea foam based on the agitation level of water, amount of organic material, and the presence of salt. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

agitation_level.description: The level of agitation in the water, represented by a scale from 1 (calm) to 10 (very agitated).

organic_material.description: The amount of organic material present in grams per liter. This is a float type value.

salt_presence.description: Indicates whether salt is present (true) or not (false) in the water.

temperature.description: The water temperature in degrees Celsius. If unspecified, defaults to average sea temperature. This is a float type value.

message.content:
The sea’s color is a dynamic, ever‑changing palette that depends on a handful of natural factors:

| Factor | How it changes the color |
|--------|--------------------------|
| **Depth** | Shallow water reflects the sky, often giving a bright turquoise or pale blue. Deeper water absorbs longer wavelengths (reds, oranges) and scatters shorter ones (blues, greens), so it looks darker, ranging from deep blue to almost black. |
| **Water clarity** | Clear, clean water lets light penetrate deeper, producing vivid blues. Turbid or algae‑rich water scatters light, turning the surface greenish‑yellow or even brownish. |
| **Sun angle & time of day** | Morning and late‑afternoon light can give the sea a golden or pinkish hue, while midday sun produces a crisp, bright blue. |
| **Atmospheric conditions** | Overcast skies diffuse light, making the sea look gray or muted. A clear sky can make it appear more vibrant. |
| **Substrate** | Sandy bottoms reflect light back up, brightening the water; rocky or vegetated bottoms can darken it. |
| **Biological activity** | Phytoplankton blooms (high chlorophyll) turn the water greenish‑blue; certain algae can even give a reddish tint. |

So, while the “color of the sea” is often described as blue, it’s really a spectrum that shifts with depth, clarity, light, and life.
